10.4 Fuel Quality Incident — Dec 13/14

On Dec 13 at 09:10, the 2,500 L delivery for Gen A & Gen B was noted in the log as
"fuel looked cloudy". Engineer Tunde Bakare was called at 09:45. He took a 1 L sample
from the delivery truck and a second sample from the Gen A day tank. The truck sample
was cloudy with a brown tint; the day tank sample was clear. Bakare instructed the
driver to hold the truck on site.

At 15:00, Bakare drained the water separator on Gen A and found approximately 200 mL
of water. The generator ran normally after this. On Dec 14 at 07:00, during the full
service, the fuel filter on Gen A was replaced. The old filter was visibly clogged
with a dark, sludgy residue. The sample from the truck was sent to Petrocam's lab on
Dec 14. Lab report is pending.

Gen A ran without interruption during the Dec 13 evening show. Gen B was not run on
Dec 13 evening. Gen C ran rough for 10 minutes on Dec 13 after start-up; this was
cleared after a filter clean and is not linked to the Main Stage fuel issue.

Action taken: Petrocam was told to send only their senior rep, T. Ibrahim, for
deliveries until the lab report is back. All future deliveries will be checked for
cloudiness before the truck is allowed to pump.

### 2.5 Fuel Storage and Handling at the Festival Site

The festival site uses a combination of generator-mounted base tanks and two bulk storage tanks located near the rear service road. The bulk tanks (Tank 1 and Tank 2) are above-ground, double-walled units with a capacity of 5,000 liters each. They are connected to the generator compound by a fixed pipe manifold. Tank 1 is used for the main supply to Stage A and Stage B generators. Tank 2 is reserved for the backup generator and the refueling of the smaller distribution units used by the food village.

The bulk tanks are equipped with a sight glass, a dipstick hatch, and a mechanical level gauge. The level gauge on Tank 2 has been known to stick at certain readings; always confirm with the dipstick before drawing fuel. The dipstick is calibrated in liters and is marked with a red paint band at the 4,000-liter level. Do not rely on the gauge alone.

**Daily fuel log procedure:**

At the start of each shift, the Gen Tech on duty records the dipstick reading for both bulk tanks in the fuel log. The log is kept in the generator compound office, on the clipboard next to the door. Readings are taken at 08:00 and 20:00 daily. Each entry must include the date, time, tank number, dipstick reading in liters, and the initials of the person taking the reading. If a delivery is made, the receipt number and batch number are entered in the remarks column.

When the dipstick reading for Tank 1 falls below 1,200 liters, the Gen Tech must notify the Logistics Coordinator by radio. The Logistics Coordinator arranges the next delivery. The festival does not keep a standing contract with a single fuel supplier for the bulk tanks; deliveries are ordered on an as-needed basis from the approved vendor list maintained in the site office.

**Fuel transfer from bulk tank to generator base tank:**

The transfer pump is located beside Tank 1. The pump is a hand-crank unit with a hose that reaches the filler necks of both the Stage A and Stage B generators. The pump is not rated for continuous duty; allow it to cool for five minutes after every 200 liters transferred. The hose end is fitted with a coarse mesh filter. The filter is cleaned at the start of each shift and after any delivery. A spare filter is kept in the parts drawer in the generator compound.

Before starting a transfer, check the fuel in the bulk tank for clarity. Draw a small sample into a clean glass jar and hold it against a white background. If the fuel looks cloudy or hazy, stop and contact the Technical Director. Do not transfer cloudy fuel into any generator tank.

**Water in fuel – detection and response:**

Water can enter the fuel system through condensation in the bulk tanks, a leaking fill cap, or a delivery that was contaminated at the source. The primary defense is the water separator / primary filter fitted to each generator. This filter is a spin-on type with a clear bowl at the bottom. The bowl allows visual inspection of any water that has settled out.

The Gen Tech on duty shall inspect the water separator bowl at the start of each shift and after every 200 liters of fuel transferred. If water is visible in the bowl, drain it using the valve at the bottom. Drain the water into a metal container, not onto the ground. Record the drainage in the fuel log under the remarks column.

If water is found in the separator bowl more than twice in a single shift, or if the fuel in the bulk tank appears hazy, the Technical Director must be notified immediately. The fuel in the affected tank shall be considered suspect and shall not be used until a sample has been tested. The sample is drawn from the bottom of the tank using the sample tap fitted to the tank drain line.

10. FUEL & GENERATOR LOG

This log is maintained by the production office. Entries are recorded at each fuel delivery and
at every generator service. Fuel deliveries are made daily by Petrocam Energy. All times are
local (WAT). Any abnormality, however small, must be noted in the Remarks column.

10.1 Daily Fuel Deliveries — Main Stage (Gen A & Gen B)

Dec 10      09:15    2,000     J. Musa         Delivery on time. Dip readings matched.

Dec 13      09:10    2,500     T. Ibrahim      Fuel looked cloudy. Sample taken, see 10.4.

----------  -------  --------  --------------  --------------------------------------------

Dec 13      10:05    1,500     P. Ade         Gen C ran rough for 10 min after start. Cleared.
Dec 14      09:30    1,500     P. Ade         Ok.

10.3 Generator Service Log

Gen     Date       Time     Hours   Service / Check            By (Engineer)
------  ---------  -------  ------  --------------------------  ---------------
Gen A   Dec 10     08:00    1,240   Pre-event service, oil     T. Bakare
                                    change, filters.
Gen B   Dec 10     08:30    1,105   Pre-event service, oil     T. Bakare
                                    change, filters.
Gen A   Dec 12     07:00    1,310   Oil top-up, belt check.    T. Bakare
Gen A   Dec 13     15:00    1,385   Checked after cloudy       T. Bakare
                                    fuel report. Drained
                                    water separator.
Gen B   Dec 13     15:30    1,150   Checked as precaution.     T. Bakare
Gen C   Dec 13     11:00    980     Checked rough run.         S. Adeyemi
                                    Cleaned fuel filter.
Gen D   Dec 13     11:20    1,020   Checked as precaution.     S. Adeyemi
Gen A   Dec 14     07:00    1,410   Full service. Replaced     T. Bakare
                                    fuel filter. See 10.4.

10.4 Fuel Quality Incident — Dec 13/14

On Dec 13 at 09:10, the 2,500 L delivery for Gen A & Gen B was noted in the log as
"fuel looked cloudy". Engineer Tunde Bakare was called at 09:45. He took a 1 L sample
from the delivery truck and a second sample from the Gen A day tank. The truck sample
was cloudy with a brown tint; the day tank sample was clear. Bakare instructed the
driver to hold the truck on site.

At 15:00, Bakare drained the water separator on Gen A and found approximately 200 mL
of water. The generator ran normally after this. On Dec 14 at 07:00, during the full
service, the fuel filter on Gen A was replaced. The old filter was visibly clogged
with a dark, sludgy residue. The sample from the truck was sent to Petrocam's lab on
Dec 14. Lab report is pending.

Gen A ran without interruption during the Dec 13 evening show. Gen B was not run on
Dec 13 evening. Gen C ran rough for 10 minutes on Dec 13 after start-up; this was
cleared after a filter clean and is not linked to the Main Stage fuel issue.

Action taken: Petrocam was told to send only their senior rep, T. Ibrahim, for
deliveries until the lab report is back. All future deliveries will be checked for
cloudiness before the truck is allowed to pump.

## Equipment Manuals – Lagos Soundwave Festival

### 2.5 Fuel Storage and Handling at the Festival Site

The festival site uses a combination of generator-mounted base tanks and two bulk storage tanks located near the rear service road. The bulk tanks (Tank 1 and Tank 2) are above-ground, double-walled units with a capacity of 5,000 liters each. They are connected to the generator compound by a fixed pipe manifold. Tank 1 is used for the main supply to Stage A and Stage B generators. Tank 2 is reserved for the backup generator and the refueling of the smaller distribution units used by the food village.

The bulk tanks are equipped with a sight glass, a dipstick hatch, and a mechanical level gauge. The level gauge on Tank 2 has been known to stick at certain readings; always confirm with the dipstick before drawing fuel. The dipstick is calibrated in liters and is marked with a red paint band at the 4,000-liter level. Do not rely on the gauge alone.

**Daily fuel log procedure:**

At the start of each shift, the Gen Tech on duty records the dipstick reading for both bulk tanks in the fuel log. The log is kept in the generator compound office, on the clipboard next to the door. Readings are taken at 08:00 and 20:00 daily. Each entry must include the date, time, tank number, dipstick reading in liters, and the initials of the person taking the reading. If a delivery is made, the receipt number and batch number are entered in the remarks column.

When the dipstick reading for Tank 1 falls below 1,200 liters, the Gen Tech must notify the Logistics Coordinator by radio. The Logistics Coordinator arranges the next delivery. The festival does not keep a standing contract with a single fuel supplier for the bulk tanks; deliveries are ordered on an as-needed basis from the approved vendor list maintained in the site office.

**Fuel transfer from bulk tank to generator base tank:**

The transfer pump is located beside Tank 1. The pump is a hand-crank unit with a hose that reaches the filler necks of both the Stage A and Stage B generators. The pump is not rated for continuous duty; allow it to cool for five minutes after every 200 liters transferred. The hose end is fitted with a coarse mesh filter. The filter is cleaned at the start of each shift and after any delivery. A spare filter is kept in the parts drawer in the generator compound.

Before starting a transfer, check the fuel in the bulk tank for clarity. Draw a small sample into a clean glass jar and hold it against a white background. If the fuel looks cloudy or hazy, stop and contact the Technical Director. Do not transfer cloudy fuel into any generator tank.

**Water in fuel – detection and response:**

Water can enter the fuel system through condensation in the bulk tanks, a leaking fill cap, or a delivery that was contaminated at the source. The primary defense is the water separator / primary filter fitted to each generator. This filter is a spin-on type with a clear bowl at the bottom. The bowl allows visual inspection of any water that has settled out.

The Gen Tech on duty shall inspect the water separator bowl at the start of each shift and after every 200 liters of fuel transferred. If water is visible in the bowl, drain it using the valve at the bottom. Drain the water into a metal container, not onto the ground. Record the drainage in the fuel log under the remarks column.

If water is found in the separator bowl more than twice in a single shift, or if the fuel in the bulk tank appears hazy, the Technical Director must be notified immediately. The fuel in the affected tank shall be considered suspect and shall not be used until a sample has been tested. The sample is drawn from the bottom of the tank using the sample tap fitted to the tank drain line.
